chunks: And it is narrated from Yūnus ibn Ya‘qūb, who said:
I said to Abī ‘Abdillāh عليه السلام: A man purchases goods from another man, then asks for them as a gift after the purchase, without compelling him.
He عليه السلام said: “There is no harm in it.”

key_terms.الْبَيْعَ: the sold goods or sale item in context
key_terms.بَعْدَ الشِّرَاءِ: after the purchase has taken place
key_terms.فَيَسْتَوْهِبُهُ: then asks for it to be given as a gift
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ بِهِ: there is no legal problem or objection in it

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible for a buyer to ask the seller to gift the sold item after the purchase without coercion?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning a sale followed by the buyer requesting the item as a gift from the seller. Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام states that there is no harm in this arrangement so long as it is done without coercion.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.3856 - It is narrated from Yunus bin Ya'qub who said:
I said to Abu Abdillah (as), "A man purchases goods from another man and then asks for them as a gift after the purchase, without compelling him."
Imam (as) said: "There is no harm in it."
